statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-15310: zipfile decompressed bzip2, LZMA and Zstandard members without a max_length bound, so a crafted archive could make Python allocate memory sized by attacker-controlled data. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/156002 (3.12 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/09a2e7e6678b4f65449e7ad8f112c48f944591e2), first released in CPython 3.12.15; see https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-15310. Checked Lib/zipfile/__init__.py for the bounded decompress(data, max_length) reads that the fix adds in the python-3.12 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4, x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. Builds before 3.12.14-r2 lack the fix; 3.12.14-r2 and every later build have it (3.12.14-r2 carries a backport made before the 3.12.15 release; 3.12.15-r0 and later ship the upstream 3.12.15 file). The range ends at 3.12.14-r2.

zipfile decompressed bzip2 and LZMA members without a max_length bound, so a crafted archive could make Python allocate memory from an attacker-controlled size. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/156002 (3.13 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/dcdd406ddbfc4cb29b24c3df17cbabe21d316ce1), first released in CPython 3.13.16; see the advisory https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/YUHXURX2WZGKGNA4ANYBQS2VZRYQ5JNK/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-15310. The DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.13 package carries a backport of that fix from 3.13.15-r2, made before the upstream 3.13.16 release; 3.13.16-r0 and later are built from CPython 3.13.16 or later (the version string in libpython3.13.so), which include it. Compared Lib/zipfile/__init__.py in the python-3.13 package in every published build on x86_64 and aarch64 (3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.18-r4) with the file in the matching upstream CPython release: 3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.15-r1 ship the upstream file unchanged, without the bounded decompress(data, max_length) path for these compression methods; 3.13.15-r2 adds it; 3.13.16-r0 and later ship the upstream 3.13.16 or later file, which has it.

CVE-2026-15310: zipfile decompressed bzip2, LZMA and Zstandard members without a max_length bound, so a crafted archive could make Python allocate memory of an attacker-controlled size. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/156002 (3.14 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/31980e84b9a708424a0a1dfecde3fc991e313f89), first released in CPython 3.14.8; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/YUHXURX2WZGKGNA4ANYBQS2VZRYQ5JNK/. A follow-up in 3.14.8 (https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/157557) only keeps monkey-patched decompressors working; https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-15310. Compared Lib/zipfile/__init__.py in every published build, 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.10-r4, of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.14 package on x86_64 and aarch64 with the files in the upstream CPython 3.14 releases. 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.7-r1 lack the fix; 3.14.7-r2 is the first published build that has it and carries a DHI backport of the upstream fix, ahead of the upstream release, and every later build carries it.
